mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in the country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, authorised representatives and material counterparties against the Financial Intelligence Centre domestic financial sanctions list, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU and UK financial sanctions lists, and Interpol and related regulatory alerts. Politically Exposed Persons must be identified on a risk-sensitive basis in accordance with FICA, with enhanced due diligence applied to source of funds, source of wealth and beneficial ownership before incorporation and throughout the banking relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC eServices - Companies and Intellectual Property Commission online company registry portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be in one of South Africa's official languages and rendered in Latin characters. If the name originates in a foreign language or script, a defensible Latin-alphabet transliteration and, where necessary, an English translation must be supplied. A private company name must end with Proprietary Limited or (Pty) Ltd and must not be misleading, offensive or in conflict with the public interest under section 11 of the Companies Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation lapses if the company is not incorporated within the reservation window. Any extension or re-use must be applied for before expiry via CIPC eServices, subject to CIPC tariff. Upon rejection, CIPC issues a refusal notice; the applicant may file a fresh name reservation or may appeal to the Companies Tribunal in accordance with Companies Regulations, 2011, regulation 142, by submitting the prescribed Companies Tribunal form and paying the prescribed filing fee. The Tribunal may confirm, set aside or remit the decision. During and after any appeal, the applicant may also apply for an alternative name without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with limitations. The registered office must be a physical South African street address capable of receiving service of legal process and inspection of statutory records; a post office box or mail-forwarding address alone is not acceptable. A registered virtual office provider may be used if it provides a verifiable street address and accepts service on behalf of the company. For a specialty green coffee bean importer, SARS, banks and documentary credit issuers will ordinarily require evidence of actual operational substance rather than a bare virtual office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; approximately 5% unannounced site inspection probability per annum for a low-risk green coffee bean import company with no adverse AML/CFT flags. The likelihood increases materially if SARS, the Financial Intelligence Centre or the designated authority identifies customs valuation discrepancies, unexplained UBO structures or lack of commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss 13, 19, 40, 66; Companies Regulations, 2011
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Department of Trade, Industry and Competition
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR14.1) together with Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a private company may incorporate with nominal or zero share capital. No escrow or proof-of-capital account is required under South African law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscribers' subscription to the authorised share capital set out in the Memorandum of Incorporation is accepted and the allotted shares are issued in accordance with section 40 of the Companies Act, 2008. 2. The company's registered office be and is hereby fixed at [Registered Address], South Africa, and the postal address is adopted for statutory service. 3. [Director Name] is appointed as Director and [Managing Director Name] as Managing Director, each authorised to open bank accounts and execute filings with CIPC, SARS, and the relevant regulatory bodies. This resolution is effective immediately and recorded in the minutes of this duly convened first board meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and MOI Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a company name search and submit a name reservation request online. Attach the proposed MOI and stakeholder consents. If the name is not reserved, select a secondary name or lodge a name objection with CIPC.
required_dossiers: Certified ID or passport copies of subscribers and directors
Notice of registered office consent form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend and resubmit the name reservation online; alternatively file a formal name-objection complaint with CIPC for adjudication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form CoR14.1 electronically via CIPC BizOnline, attaching the MOI and the name reservation certificate. Pay the prescribed registration fee. Upon registration, CIPC issues a Certificate of Incorporation and a company registration number.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and postal address
Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to CIPC compliance queries by amending the CoR14.1 or MOI and resubmitting through the same portal; escalation to CIPC Contact Centre if processing exceeds published service standards.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF); Compensation Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax and obtain an income tax number. Register for VAT if taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed the ZAR 1 million threshold. Register as an employer with SARS, UIF, and the Compensation Fund for COIDA compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Follow SARS escalation procedure through eFiling disputes and revisit registration submissions; correct filing errors and resubmit to the relevant registration branch.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business License and Customs Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Metropolitan Municipality Business Licensing Department; SARS Customs and Excise
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence under the Business Act 71 of 1991 or the applicable municipal by-law. Obtain a zoning certificate confirming the property permits warehousing and wholesale distribution. Register with SARS Customs as a importer to enable documentary LC and import releases for green coffee beans.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of owners or managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Lodge a written objection or appeal with the municipal licensing authority; remedy zoning shortfalls by filing a use-application; coordinate with a clearing agent to correct customs registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical, Environmental and Occupational Clearance Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment; Local Fire Authority; Department of Employment and Labour Inspectorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a site environmental screening to confirm the wholesale handling of green coffee does not trigger a listed environmental activity. Obtain a fire safety certificate for the warehouse. Complete an OHSA risk assessment and secure a structural load certificate for racking and storage areas.
required_dossiers: Site plan and lease or ownership deed
Occupational Health and Safety risk assessment
Structural engineer certificate for racking and load-bearing areas
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remediate any fire or OHSA findings and request a reinspection; submit rectified environmental reports to DFFE; apply for an exemption or mitigation plan where industrial thresholds are inadvertently triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Business Licensing Department and Department of Employment and Labour; SARS Customs for trade licensing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Trading Licence under the Business Act 71 of 1991 and SARS Customs Client Registration for imported green coffee

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Registration/Exemption: listed activity not triggered for low-impact wholesale and warehousing of green coffee beans; waste registration applies only if hazardous waste storage or disposal thresholds are exceeded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Green coffee handling is assessed against National Water Act discharge requirements; stormwater must not contain measurable pollutants; no significant VOC or particulate emissions are expected from unroasted bean handling. Waste packaging must be separated and disposed of in accordance with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act duty-of-care obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the local municipal fire authority under the National Building Regulations; structural load certificate for warehouse racking; OHSA risk assessment and clearance from the Department of Employment and Labour for workplace health and safety compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — SARS eFiling portal (www.sarsefiling.co.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-incorporated entities act through a registered representative in South Africa. File SARS company income tax registration via eFiling or at a SARS branch using the Companies and Close Corporations Registration form (CoR 14.1 extract from CIPC plus Application for Registration for Income Tax – new entity). Obtain an Income Tax Reference Number (tax reference number) before trading. Separately register for VAT under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991 on VAT101 form (compulsory once taxable supply turnover exceeds ZAR 1,000,000 in 12 months, or voluntary above ZAR 50,000 in 12 months). All registrations require a board resolution, proof of registered address, and identity/authority documentation for directors.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a check-the-box pass-through regime. A (Pty) Ltd is a separate taxable person subject to normal tax at the entity level. Elective mechanisms available include VAT group registration (section 50 of the VAT Act) for wholly-owned groups, election for income tax deductibility of certain financial instruments, and the option to apply the South African residence basis of taxation if the entity is effectively managed in South Africa. No hybrid mismatch elections are separately available beyond the anti-avoidance provisions aligned with the OECD BEPS framework.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 compulsory taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary registration permitted if supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 in 12 months; registration may also be required for suppliers of imported services engaged in non-taxable activities if nexus criteria are met
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime. SARS accepts electronic tax invoices and requires electronic filing of VAT201 returns through eFiling or an approved software integrator. Tax invoices must contain prescribed particulars including supplier/recipient VAT numbers, description, date, price, and VAT charged. SARS is advancing an eInvoicing framework but there is currently no statutory obligation for pre-clearance or digital fiscal validation at the border.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act where goods are supplied by the vendor to a non-resident recipient, supplied under a sale or consignment, and exported from South Africa within 60 days (or further period approved by SARS) of the date of supply. Alternatively, under section 11(1)(b), a supply of movable goods is zero-rated where the goods are supplied to an exporter vendor and are exported within 90 days (or approved extended period) from the date of supply. The supplier must retain evidence showing the physical export and that the goods left the Republic. Services exported to non-residents may also be zero-rated if attributable to a non-resident location of supply and not for use in South Africa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500), Bill of Lading (or Airwaybill), Inward Remittance Certificate or bank settlement statement evidencing receipt of foreign currency, signed commercial invoice, packing list, and a statement by the exporting agent confirming physical removal from South Africa
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may audit zero-rated export supplies within a five-year prescription period. Failure to hold sufficient documentary proof results in the adjustment of VAT to 15% with additional tax, interest, and understatement penalties up to 100% of the shortfall depending on behaviour. Deliberate fraudulent zero-rating claims attract criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act, fines, and imprisonment. Misdeclared exports can also be clawed back with retrospective effect from the date of supply, and exchange-control violations for late repatriation may trigger separate administrative penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933), the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, and the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorized Dealers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand (ZAR) is a free-floating currency with full current-account convertibility for bona fide trade transactions: import payments for green coffee, freight, insurance, and incidental processing services may be routed without FinSurv pre-approval through any Authorized Dealer, subject only to standard documentary verification (SAD500 customs declaration, commercial invoice, contract, bill of lading). Capital-account convertibility is restricted: inward foreign direct investment into a South African (Pty) Ltd is freely permitted but must be declared to and recorded by the Authorized Dealer; outward direct investments, offshore bank accounts, and foreign borrowings by the local company require Authorized Dealer approval within the annual discretionary allowances (outward FDI allowance is ZAR 10 million per legal entity per calendar year) or FinSurv approval above those limits. Profit and dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted without SARB pre-approval provided the company holds verifiably distributable reserves evidenced by audited financial statements; the remittance is subject to the 20% dividend withholding tax under Section 64E-64H of the Income Tax Act, and in bank practice depends on the inward-foreign-investment reference being correctly recorded at the time of capital injection. Practical hurdles: post-FATF-grey-listing compliance is strict, bank onboarding timelines for non-resident-owned commodity traders are materially longer, any capital inflow not tagged with the inward-investment reference blocks future dividend and exit remittances, and prohibited loop structures (South African funds diverted offshore and returned as FDI) attract severe penalties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Exchange Control Regulation 6 read with the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual - Exporters, all export proceeds must be received in South Africa within 30 days of the date of shipment, unless the Authorized Dealer has approved extended payment terms up to 12 months, or FinSurv has approved terms beyond 12 months. On receipt, 100% of the foreign-currency export proceeds must be surrendered to an Authorized Dealer, meaning sold to the Authorized Dealer for ZAR at the ruling market rate; alternatively, if the exporter maintains a permitted Foreign Currency Account, the proceeds may be retained in that account strictly for permissible current-account trade disbursements such as payment to foreign suppliers, freight, insurance, and other trade-related services. There is no fractional mandatory conversion ratio: surrender is effectively 100% unless the Foreign Currency Account route is used, and the exporter must complete the Authorized Dealer's export declaration, retain shipment evidence (bill of lading, SAD500), and report outstanding export proceeds if payment is not received within the 30-day window. For ZA_PTY_LTD, this rule is operationally relevant only if the company re-exports green coffee to SADC/SACU markets via the SIRESS clearing system or undertakes a back-to-back container re-shipment; if the company imports only for local distribution, the corollary obligation is full compliance with import-payment timing and documentation rules enforced by the Authorized Dealer.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational ZAR Account with linked Capital Escrow / Inward Foreign Investment ledger
Operational ZAR Account and Foreign Currency Account for trade settlements
Capital Escrow Account for inward FDI and Operational Account
Operational Account with Trade Finance / Import Letter of Credit sub-limits

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low for use as the primary treasury or clearing rail; Medium only as an ancillary receivables-collection tool that is swept daily into the Authorized Dealer. Legal constraints: offshore digital EMIs (Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer, Intergiro, BCB Group) do not hold South African Authorized Dealer licences; they cannot receive export-proceeds surrenders, cannot issue valid SARB balance-of-payments purpose codes, and cannot maintain the inward-foreign-investment reference required for future dividend remittances. Additionally, a South African-resident company is prohibited under Exchange Control Regulation 10 from holding any offshore bank or EMI account without prior SARB FinSurv approval. The compliant alternative is the Authorized Dealer's own multi-currency digital platform, which delivers comparable speed, upfront pricing, and API connectivity while preserving exchange-control legality.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is near-mandatory in the post-FATF-grey-listing environment. FICA as amended by the General Laws Amendment Act 22 of 2022 requires full customer due diligence on every director and every beneficial owner holding 25% or more of ZA_PTY_LTD. All four Tier-1 banks require at least one director, or a formally appointed local operator holding a notarised power of attorney, to attend an in-person interview at a South African branch when opening the corporate account and activating digital banking channels. Non-resident directors may complete non-face-to-face identification via the bank's video-based e-KYC where policy allows, but the account-opening board resolution, constitutional documents, and individual identity documents must be original, notarially certified, and apostilled, or conformed copies at the bank's discretion. A fully remote opening is theoretically possible but rarely granted to non-resident-owned commodity traders given the grey-list and the enhanced scrutiny required by FATF Recommendations 15 and 22. The practical recommendation is to appoint a South African resident director or company secretary before onboarding so that the physical interview, FICA sign-off, and account activation can be completed in a two-to-four-week window.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial-ownership concentration: sole shareholder or director resident outside South Africa with no local tax profile, triggering Enhanced Due Diligence and Politically Exposed Person checks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised passport copies; apostilled proof of residential address; three months of personal bank statements from the investor's home bank; signed source-of-wealth affidavit; business profile and curriculum vitae; CIPC share register extract; beneficial-ownership chart for every UBO holding 25% or more; tax-residence certificate; professional introduction letter from the investor's existing relationship bank; and a FICA-compliant declaration of the source of the inbound investment funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering flags: repeated advance payments to green-coffee suppliers in Colombia, Ethiopia, or Brazil with unit pricing outside the ICE benchmark tolerance and no transport-document trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Green Coffee Association master contract with clear Incoterms; supplier proforma and final invoices; ICE 'C' futures benchmark price tick plus regional differential used for pricing; third-party pre-shipment survey certificate (SGS, Cotecna, or Bureau Veritas) covering grade and weight; original negotiable bill of lading; SAD500 export or import declarations; marine cargo insurance with the company named as assured; bank-to-bank trade reference; and the Authorized Dealer's exchange-control clearance record for the underlying import.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment-routing anomaly: a supplier instruction directs settlement to a third-country shell entity or to a director's personal account, violating know-your-transaction principles and creating fraud or money-laundering red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written payment-redirection instruction on the supplier's letterhead signed by the supplier's managing director; banking confirmation that the receiving account is owned by the named payee; underlying supply contract with a valid receivables assignment clause; group-structure chart demonstrating the affiliation of the third-country entity; internal board minutes approving the deviation; enhanced KYC file on the actual payee including corporate-registry searches and sanctions or PEP screening results; and a repayment undertaking if funds are held under a trust or escrow arrangement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return including BE-10 Public Interest Score declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation each year; 40-business-day grace period before late penalties accrue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalties ZAR 100-500 per outstanding year (category/income-based); failure to file for two consecutive years triggers a CIPC final demand letter and administrative strike-off (deregistration). Directors become jointly and severally liable for debts contracted after deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation attached to the Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted annually together with the CIPC Annual Return; any change in beneficial ownership must be lodged with CIPC within 10 business days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to ZAR 1,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; directors jointly liable; false or incomplete UBO data is a criminal offence with imprisonment up to 10 years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after financial year end (default FYE 28/29 February; return due by the same date in the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% of assessed tax for late or non-submission; escalating monthly administrative non-compliance penalties up to ZAR 16,000 for large-turnover entities; SARS may raise a deemed/estimated assessment with interest at the prescribed rate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provisional Tax Returns (IRP6) - first, second and voluntary top-up estimates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First estimate: 6 months after year-of-assessment start (31 August for 28 February year-end); second estimate: last day of the tax year (28/29 February); top-up estimate: within 6 months of year-end (30 September)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest at the prescribed rate (repo + 3%) compounded from the statutory due date; additional 20% tax on the understated amount where the second estimate is less than 80% of actual taxable income.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer annual reconciliation (EMP501) for PAYE, UIF and Skills Development Levy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Period 1 (1 March - 31 August): by 31 October; Period 2 (1 September - 28/29 February): by 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment penalty on undisclosed PAYE/UIF/SDL plus prescribed-rate interest; monthly administrative penalties for late or non-submission; directors personally liable for unremitted employee taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: B-BBEE annual compliance certificate (Qualifying Small Enterprise) or exempt micro-enterprise affidavit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after financial year end; affidavit executed by an accounting officer for turnover under ZAR 10 million; SANAS-accredited certificate required for turnover ZAR 10-50 million
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Not a tax filing; absence of a valid B-BBEE level excludes the entity from state procurement and sector licences; false declarations attract fines up to 10% of annual turnover or imprisonment up to 10 years.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent audit if the company's Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more, or if it is a public or state-owned company, or its MOI so requires. PIS is calculated on the BE-10 basis: 1 point per employee, 1 point per R1 million (or part) of third-party liabilities, 1 point per R1 million (or part) of turnover, plus 1 point per individual holding a direct or indirect beneficial interest in shares. PIS 100-349 requires an independent review; PIS below 100 is exempt from external audit or review unless the MOI demands otherwise.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in South Africa for public-interest entities and companies with PIS >= 350; IFRS for SMEs for private companies with PIS < 350. Financial statements are prepared under section 29 of the Companies Act 71/2008, and the ITR14 reconciles accounting profit to taxable income under the Income Tax Act 58/1962.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: CIPC requires every Pty Ltd to file a beneficial-ownership confirmation annually with the Annual Return, identifying all natural persons holding a beneficial interest of >= 5% or exercising effective control (directly or via nominees or trusts). Any shareholding transfer or ownership change must be updated in the company's Beneficial Ownership Register and lodged with CIPC within 10 business days; the annual confirmation must reconcile all register transfers made during the year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Prescribed Officers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 190-810 (ZAR 3,500-15,000) per year for a registered office address and corporate secretarial agent, depending on service scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,700-8,100 (ZAR 50,000-150,000) for a full statutory audit; USD 1,100-3,200 (ZAR 20,000-60,000) for an independent review in audit-exempt companies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023 (28% for years ending before that date)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific incentive for green coffee distribution. General reliefs: Small Business Corporation graduated rates (0% on first ZAR 95,500; 7% to ZAR 191,000; 21% to ZAR 336,000; 27% above) if the Pty Ltd is held exclusively by natural persons with annual turnover below ZAR 20 million; section 12B accelerated capital allowance for qualifying energy assets; section 11D 150% R&D deduction; Employment Tax Incentive for qualifying wages. A plain wholesale distribution entity will effectively bear the headline 27%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory expiry — assessed losses carry forward indefinitely; however, for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 January 2022, only 80% of an assessed loss may be set off against taxable income in any year, with the unutilised balance carried forward without a time limit
